observations: Torah #110 is a very short teaching (3 lines) about free choice (bechira). It contains no bechina-type identifications — no language like 'X הוא בחינת Y' or 'X נקרא Y'. The teaching makes a single philosophical assertion (free choice is always available) and explains why people are confused (habit from youth). The relationship between habit and the illusion of lacking free choice is causal (eitza), not shared-nature (bechina). With only 2 concepts and no bechina connections between them, no new package can be proposed (minimum threshold: 3 bechina-connected nodes forming an independent domain). No evil mirror structure is present.
